collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 5-13)

collection.description: A child cast as the First Fire in the founding play wants a bigger part: give them a bigger part, or explain why the fire matters.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Every year, the children put on a play about the founding of the village: the first canoe landing, the first fire, the first hut. (subject) is in charge this year. (friend) has been cast as the First Fire, which mostly involves waving orange leaves. (friend.He/she) wants a bigger part.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) adds a new character: the First Crab, who greets the founders on the beach. (friend) is thrilled. On the night, (friend.he/she) scuttles out sideways and announces, "Welcome to Isola! I am the crab!" in such a huge voice that the audience collapses. It is not historically accurate. It's the best part of the play. The First Crab is in every play after that.

text_only.reason: a small thing breaks in the story; no building is damaged -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) tells (friend) that without the First Fire, there'd be no cooking, no warmth, no light, no village. (friend) considers this. On the night, (friend.he/she) waves (friend.his/her) leaves with tremendous intensity, crackling and hissing, for the entire play, including several scenes where the fire is not supposed to be lit. It's very distracting. Everyone agrees it's the most committed fire they've ever seen.
